keyword: how long will it take artemis 2 to reach the moon

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is expected to reach the vicinity of the Moon on the sixth day of their mission, likely around April 6 or 7, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'On Monday, it will reach the moon'; 'reach the moon in five days, by Monday night' (launch Wed April 1, Monday=April 6); R3: 'day six of the mission—Monday, April 6'; R6: 'get to the moon on the sixth day'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm sixth day arrival around April 6 post-April 1 launch.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft will not enter orbit.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'placed the spacecraft in a large looping orbit'; 'high-Earth orbit'; R3: 'won’t even orbit the moon' (specifies lunar); but enters Earth orbit
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm entry into high Earth orbit before TLI; claim absolute, contradicts without lunar qualifier.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft will make a single, high-altitude loop approximately 4,000 to 5,000 miles above the lunar surface.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'fly within about 4,000 miles above the surface'; 'more than 4,100 miles'; R3: '4,000 miles'; R5: '5,000 miles (8,000 kilometers)'; R6: 'at least 4,000 nautical miles'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state single flyby/loop at 4,000-5,000 miles altitude.

verifications.claim: NASA and CNN state that the total mission length is approximately 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: NASA and CNN sources explicitly state ~10 days.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft will utilize a free-return trajectory.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'free return trajectory'; R2: 'free-return trajectory'; R3: 'free-return trajectory'; R5: 'free-return trajectory'; R7: 'free-return trajectory'
verifications.reasoning: All major sources confirm free-return trajectory.

verifications.claim: A free-return trajectory relies on Earth's gravity to slow the spacecraft down over the course of the journey.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'uses the moon’s gravity to swing the capsule directly back'; R2: 'use the moon’s gravity to fling itself back'; R3: 'moon’s gravity palming the spacecraft [...] flinging it straight back'
verifications.reasoning: Sources emphasize moon's gravity for return; Earth's gravity slows outbound/inbound but not defining feature of free-return.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will travel around the far side of the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'passing over the far side'; R2: 'journey around the moon'; R3: 'around the far side of the moon'; R5: 'lunar far side'
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of far side flyby.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will reach a point farther from Earth than any previous human mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'set a distance record [...] 252,799 miles, or 4,144 miles farther than Apollo 13'; R2: 'travel farther from Earth than any human ever has'; R3: 'farther from Earth than any person has ever ventured'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state new distance record beyond Apollo 13.

verifications.claim: After the flyby, the Artemis II crew will return to Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'make the journey back'; R2: 'bring the crew back to Earth'; R3: 'come straight back'
verifications.reasoning: All sources describe flyby then direct return.

verifications.claim: The total journey will last about 9 to 10 days before splashing down.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown [...] on April 10' (launch April 1); R2: '10 days'; R3: '10-day journey'; R7: 'nine days, one hour and 46 minutes [...] 10-day mission'

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is a test flight designed to test the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion spacecraft with a human crew for the first time.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'check that the spacecraft can safely make the journey'; R3: 'shakedown mission test-flying the Orion spacecraft'; R4: 'first time humans have headed to the Moon [...] first crewed flight'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe as first crewed test of SLS/Orion.
